definition: Increasing the density of a 3D point cloud while preserving geometry — the 3D analogue of image super-resolution.
details: Increasing the density of a 3D point cloud while preserving geometry — the 3D analogue of image super-resolution.

explainer.lead: Point cloud super resolution increases point density while keeping the underlying geometry intact, filling in sparse scans. It matters because LiDAR and depth sensors often return far fewer points than downstream tasks need.

tiers.eli5: It's like taking a blurry dot drawing of an object and adding more dots in the gaps so the shape looks smooth.
tiers.practitioner: Applied to upscale sparse LiDAR or RGB-D captures before segmentation or registration. A pitfall is upsampling noise or outliers along with real surface detail.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a sparse point set, the task learns a mapping to a denser set that approximates the same underlying surface; it is evaluated with density-aware metrics plus geometric error such as Chamfer distance. Success is bounded by the information in the input, so genuinely missing geometry cannot be recovered.

explainer.example: A 1,024-point scan of a car part is upsampled to 8,192 points that still follow the original surface contours.
